name: PR Readiness
author: SerroAI
description: Judge a PR against what the program already knows: open risks, committed customer requirements, recorded decisions and open action items. Not a style review — a "does this land safely in this program" review.

name: Release Readiness
author: SerroAI
description: Program-level go/no-go. Surfaces committed-but-unshipped customer requirements, unresolved risks, release-gating action items and contradicted decisions, with an explicit list of what could not be checked.

name: Design PR Review
author: SerroAI
description: Review a PR against the design source of truth — a design.md, a PRD, or a Serro-linked design doc — plus the program's recorded design decisions. Reports contradictions, decision reversals, silent extensions and stale design.

name: Context Pack
author: SerroAI
description: Compile the program's live context into a committed SERRO-CONTEXT.md, so any agent — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Codepress — inherits it as ordinary repository context. Ships the serro-context skill alongside it.

name: Daily Brief
author: SerroAI
description: Pull today's meetings, recent Jira movement and open decisions from Serro and synthesise them into a short, skimmable brief. When Serro is unreachable it reports the error and returns nothing rather than filling the gap — an empty brief beats an invented one.

name: Digest Builder
author: SerroAI
description: Pull a week of program activity from Serro — meetings, Jira movement, Slack discussion, open risks and decisions — and synthesise a skimmable digest. The weekly, program-scoped counterpart to Daily Brief.

name: Effort Analysis
author: SerroAI
description: Classify a time window of engineering effort into new capability, keep-the-lights-on, internal platform and quality investment, broken down per engineer and per workstream. Reads Jira activity, repo activity, code history and the work-mix data from Serro.

name: SOP Writer
author: SerroAI
description: Gather the meeting, Slack and Jira context around an incident from Serro, run a five-whys root-cause analysis, and draft a structured SOP. Publishing to Confluence sits behind an explicit approval gate.
